newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SOCCER-FARCE IN ESTONIA HAS PRECEDENT IN CHILE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FARCE IN ESTONIA HAS PRECEDENT IN CHILE.

text.p: The Estonia-Scotland World Cup qualifier, abandoned on Wednesday after only three seconds with the home side absent without leave, is not the first game to end in such farcical circumstances.
In November 1973 Chile were due to face the old Soviet Union in a World Cup play-off in Santiago. But only the Chileans turned up.
The Soviet side had topped their European group by beating the Republic of Ireland and France while the Chileans had beaten Peru in the South American qualifiers.
The two sides played out a goalless draw in the first leg of a play-off in Moscow to decide who would qualify for the World Cup finals in West Germany the following year.
The Soviet Union were due to travel to the Chilean capital for the second leg but refused to go for political reasons.

A military coup had toppled Chile's socialist government the previous year and the match had been scheduled for Chile's national stadium, the scene of extensive human rights abuses under the new hardline regime.
The Chileans turned up, kicked off, and played towards an empty goal for a few seconds before the referee brought proceedings to a halt.
Chile were awarded the match and qualified for the finals. They were knocked out in the first round after failing to win a match.
